title: The second check on a taught word
statement: Whether a taught word's second check should be another usage item or give the meaning and ask which word fits, testing knowing in the other direction, is unsettled.
example: Three built lessons swapped the design's second usage item for one that gives the meaning and asks for the word.
detail: A reading unit's designs gave each taught word two usage items, the second as a second chance and a clean measure (`grade3-reading/artifacts/pp2-v3-design.txt`, line 54). The built lessons replaced the second with an item that states the meaning and asks which word says it, under a build-spec ruling that the two forms must do different jobs: the first tests recognising the word used correctly in a real situation, the second going from the definition back to the word (`grade3-reading/artifacts/screen-narratives/L6-NARRATIVE.md`, lines 125-130). Conformance audits recorded the swap in three lessons, and one called it an authored, self-documented adaptation of the same construct (`grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/L5.md`, line 21; `grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/L6.md`, line 139; `grade3-reading/artifacts/arc-audit/L7.md`, line 32).
against: Two rules on record would bar the meaning-to-word form: a question on a taught word must never define the word in the question (Don't define the word being tested), and a check must put the word in a new situation (Test a taught word somewhere new). Within the course a ruling settled it for the built lessons: "two vocab forms must do DIFFERENT jobs." (`grade3-reading/artifacts/screen-narratives/L6-NARRATIVE.md`, lines 127-128).

evidence.quote: Doc's Form 2 is a second usage-discrimination sentence (knight/dragon). Delivered Form 2 (`vocab-form2`) is a definition-recall MCQ ("You win a great victory after a hard struggle. Which word says that?").
Form 2 changed from usage to definition-recall per spec's "two different jobs" ruling
Form 2 tests whether the child can go from the definition back to the word — two different directions of knowing.
This is an authored, self-documented adaptation, not a silent drift — **defensible**, same assessed construct (word meaning) via a different item shape.
FORM 2 (second chance / clean measure) — Stem: Which sentence uses the word menacing correctly?
